guideline: Participants took cloze tests generated by different systems; researchers measured validity (Pearson correlation with reference tests) and reliability (Spearman-Brown split-half correlation).

Participants answered the generated cloze tests; measures of accuracy, Pearson correlation with teacher-created tests (validity), Spearman-Brown split-half reliability (internal consistency), and Discrimination Index were used.

Validity is whether a test measures the phenomenon it is intended to measure. In this case, the phenomenon is reading comprehension. To measure this, we look at Pearson correlation of nCloze scores with teacher-created cloze tests. Reliability is whether repeated testing gives similar results. When participants are only sampled once, internal consistency is used.
